posts.title: Why we keep the room open at 15:00
posts.excerpt: Most dining rooms close between lunch and dinner. Ours turns quiet instead, and the afternoon plate is the reason.
posts.content:
Most city dining rooms close their doors after the last lunch table and open again at six. We tried that in our first winter and disliked it: the room sat dark and the linen sat folded while the street outside was still busy.

So from 14:30 to 18:00 Kohaku keeps a different pace. Daniel Okafor’s team resets the room, Kenji Albrecht-Mori sends out coffee and something small from the pastry bench, and Amara Osei cooks one afternoon plate for €16. Tables of four or fewer need no booking.

People use the hours in their own way: a book, a laptop, a slow meeting with a colleague. The room is the same room, only the light is lower and nobody is counting covers. At 18:00 the dinner service begins and the lamps come up.

posts.title: Autumn on the pass
posts.excerpt: What changes on the pass when the nights draw in: brown butter, roasted fish and a heavier hand with the lamps.
posts.content:
The first cold week changes the pass before it changes the menu. Tomasz Lindqvist moves the heat lamps lower, the plates come out darker and warmer, and the brown butter gets a little more time in the pan.

This month the dinner à la carte carries a roast fish with brown butter and thyme, served on dark stoneware so the sauce looks like what it is. Mains start at €24, and the counter menu at the pass, six courses for €78, follows the same plates in smaller portions.

Lucía Ferreira has matched the fish with two whites and a light red from the glass list. Ask at the bar; she will pour a taste before you decide.

posts.title: The late sitting playlist
posts.excerpt: Low volume, long tracks: how the room sounds after 22:00, and why the playlist changes every Monday.
posts.content:
At 22:00 the late sitting begins and the room changes its voice. The lamps drop, the candles go on the tables, and the music turns from lunchtime brightness to something slower and quieter.

Daniel Okafor keeps the playlist: long tracks, few words, nothing that asks to be listened to. It is set once a week and shared in the Monday letter, so regulars can hear what is coming before they book.

The late-sitting menu is three courses for €52. The kitchen takes last orders at 23:15, and the room closes at midnight.
